subject: business-studies
description: Business Studies skill tree, FET (Amended CAPS, Business Studies Grades 10-12). Grade 10 first as proof. 4 CAPS knowledge areas (Business environment, Business venture, Business role, Business operation), each weighted 25%. Tiers = CAPS terms within a grade (T1-T4). 21 atomic skills (Grade 10). Mastery = 60% of a 20-item pool (FET rule, no timer). PROGRESSION-GATED: each skill lists the previous CAPS-order skill as a prerequisite, so the tree surfaces the current skill plus the upcoming (locked) ones. Input types: choice, true-false, cloze, sequence, image-match (existing) + sort-buckets, highlight-source, argument-builder, paragraph-template, source-comparison (tap-based mechanics, no free-text). Questions live in data/business-studies-question-bank.json. All three FET grades authored: Grade 10 (21 skills), Grade 11 (19 skills, 4 terms) and Grade 12 (15 skills, 3 teaching terms; term 4 is exam revision). Each grade is entered independently by self-reported grade and progression-gated within the grade in CAPS teaching order.

levels.title: Grade 10 — Business Studies
levels.description: Foundations across all four CAPS knowledge areas. T1: business environments (micro/market/macro), the eight business functions, quality, and business sectors. T2: contemporary socio-economic issues, social responsibility, entrepreneurial qualities, forms of ownership. T3: creative thinking & problem-solving, business opportunity & SWOT, location, contracts, presentation, the business plan. T4: self-management and team performance. 21 atomic skills, progression-gated in CAPS teaching order.

atomic_skills.title: The micro (internal) environment
atomic_skills.description: Components and features of the micro environment the business controls: vision, mission statement, goals and objectives, organisational culture, organisational resources (human, physical, financial, information) and the business organisational structure. Why the micro environment is the one level management directly controls.

error_signatures.description: Confuses vision (long-term aspiration) with mission (what the business does now)
error_signatures.example: Says a mission statement describes where the business wants to be in 20 years

error_signatures.description: Places market/macro factors inside the micro environment
error_signatures.example: Lists competitors as part of the micro environment

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The micro environment is INSIDE the business and management CONTROLS it: vision, mission, goals, culture, resources, structure. If management cannot directly change it, it is not micro.

atomic_skills.title: The eight business functions
atomic_skills.description: Identification and brief description of the eight business functions — general management, purchasing, production, marketing, public relations, human resources, administration and financing — and how they are interrelated and operate in small, medium and big businesses.

error_signatures.description: Matches a task to the wrong function
error_signatures.example: Says paying salaries is the purchasing function

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Tie each task to its function by its core purpose: purchasing buys stock, production makes the product, marketing sells it, HR manages people, finance handles money, admin handles information, PR manages image, general management coordinates all.

atomic_skills.title: Levels and tasks of general management
atomic_skills.description: The three levels of general management (top, middle, lower) and their responsibilities, plus the management tasks (planning, organising, activating/leading, controlling). The alignment between the levels and the link between good management and business success.

error_signatures.description: Confuses the management LEVEL with the management TASK
error_signatures.example: Says 'planning' is a level of management

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Levels = WHO (top/middle/lower). Tasks = WHAT every manager does (plan, organise, lead, control). Top management plans long-term; lower management supervises day-to-day.

atomic_skills.title: Quality and the business functions
atomic_skills.description: The concept of quality and how it applies to each business function (quality products, quality administration, a healthy financial function, quality management and a quality business image). The link between quality and a business achieving its objectives.

error_signatures.description: Treats quality as relevant only to the product, not to every function
error_signatures.example: Says only the production function is responsible for quality

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Quality is everyone's job. Each function has a quality measure: production = defect-free goods, finance = accurate records, HR = skilled staff, PR = good image. Poor quality in any one drags the whole business down.

atomic_skills.title: The market environment
atomic_skills.description: Components of the market environment: the market (consumers/customers), suppliers, intermediaries, competitors and other organisations (CBOs, NGOs, regulators, strategic allies, unions). The opportunities and threats these create — and that the business has no direct control over them.

error_signatures.description: Believes the business controls the market environment
error_signatures.example: Says a business can control what its competitors do

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The market environment is OUTSIDE but CLOSE: suppliers, customers, competitors, intermediaries. The business can INFLUENCE it (e.g. negotiate, advertise) but cannot CONTROL it.

atomic_skills.title: The macro environment
atomic_skills.description: Components and features of the macro environment: physical/natural, economic, social/cultural/demographic, technological, legal/political, international/global and institutional. The business has no control over these and must adapt to them.

error_signatures.description: Places a market-environment factor (e.g. a supplier) in the macro environment
error_signatures.example: Lists a single competitor as a macro-environment component

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The macro environment is the BIG outside world — the economy, laws, technology, society. The business has NO control and can only adapt. Market factors are specific people/firms; macro factors are broad forces.

atomic_skills.title: How the three environments interrelate
atomic_skills.description: The relationship between the micro, market and macro environments and the degree of control over each (full control over micro, influence over market, no control over macro). How changes in one environment ripple into the others.

error_signatures.description: Treats the three environments as separate and unconnected
error_signatures.example: Says a macro change (e.g. interest rates) cannot affect the micro environment

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Control decreases as you move outward: micro (control) → market (influence) → macro (no control). The three are connected: a macro change (e.g. a new law) forces the business to change its micro decisions.

atomic_skills.title: Business sectors
atomic_skills.description: Classification of industries into primary, secondary and tertiary sectors; the difference between the formal and informal sectors; and the difference between the public and private sectors.

error_signatures.description: Puts a manufacturing activity in the primary sector
error_signatures.example: Classifies a bakery (turns flour into bread) as primary

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Primary = extract raw materials (mining, farming). Secondary = make/process them (factories). Tertiary = services (shops, banks, transport). Formal vs informal = registered & taxed vs not. Public vs private = government-owned vs privately owned.

tiers.title: Term 2 — Socio-economic issues, social responsibility, entrepreneurship & ownership

atomic_skills.title: Contemporary socio-economic issues
atomic_skills.description: Identification and discussion of contemporary socio-economic issues that impact on business: inclusivity, unemployment, the skills levy, poverty, HIV/Aids, gambling, violence, riots/strikes, piracy (copyright, patent, trademark), counterfeiting/bootlegging and crime — and their effects on business.

error_signatures.description: Cannot connect a socio-economic issue to its concrete business impact
error_signatures.example: Says HIV/Aids has no effect on a business

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Every socio-economic issue hits business through cost or productivity: crime raises security costs, HIV/Aids reduces the labour force, strikes stop production, piracy steals sales.

atomic_skills.title: Social responsibility & CSR
atomic_skills.description: What social responsibility means and the definition of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR). Ways a business can responsibly contribute to its immediate community, and initiatives businesses take to address socio-economic issues.

error_signatures.description: Confuses social responsibility (voluntary giving back) with simply obeying the law
error_signatures.example: Says paying tax is an example of CSR

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Social responsibility = a business voluntarily giving back to society and the environment, beyond what the law requires. CSR = the company-wide programme that does this (e.g. funding a school, cleaning a river).

atomic_skills.title: Entrepreneurial qualities
atomic_skills.description: Identification of entrepreneurial qualities: desire for responsibility, risk-taking, perseverance, good management and leadership, confidence, high energy, passion, a clear vision, organisational skills, commitment and flexibility (ability to adapt).

error_signatures.description: Confuses a personal quality with a business resource
error_signatures.example: Lists 'lots of money' as an entrepreneurial quality

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Entrepreneurial qualities are personal characteristics, not resources: how the person thinks and behaves (risk-taking, perseverance, vision) — not what they own.

atomic_skills.title: Forms of ownership: sole trader & partnership
atomic_skills.description: Definition, characteristics, advantages and disadvantages of the sole proprietor and the partnership, and the differences between them — focusing on capital, liability, continuity, taxation and division of profits.

error_signatures.description: Believes a sole trader has limited liability
error_signatures.example: Says a sole trader's house is safe if the business has debts

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Sole trader and partnership both have UNLIMITED liability (owners are personally liable for debts) and no separate legal identity. Partnerships add more capital and shared skills but also shared liability.

atomic_skills.title: Forms of ownership: companies, CC & co-operatives
atomic_skills.description: Definition, characteristics, advantages and disadvantages of the close corporation, non-profit company, profit companies (private, personal liability, public, state-owned) and co-operatives — focusing on legal personality, limited liability, capital and taxation.

error_signatures.description: Thinks a private company can sell shares to the public
error_signatures.example: Says a (Pty) Ltd can list on the JSE

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A company is a separate legal person with limited liability. Private (Pty) Ltd cannot sell shares to the public; public (Ltd) can. No NEW close corporations can be registered (Companies Act 71 of 2008), but existing ones continue.

tiers.title: Term 3 — Creative thinking, opportunity, location, contracts, presentation & the business plan

atomic_skills.title: Creative thinking & problem-solving
atomic_skills.description: How creative thinking contributes to sustainable business practice; the problem-solving cycle (identify, define, formulate strategy, implement, allocate resources, monitor, evaluate); problem-solving versus decision-making; and techniques (brainstorming, mind-mapping, Delphi, Nominal Group, Force-Field Analysis, Forced Combinations).

error_signatures.description: Confuses problem-solving (finding solutions to a problem) with decision-making (choosing between options)
error_signatures.example: Treats the two terms as identical

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Problem-solving is the full cycle of fixing a problem; decision-making is one step inside it (choosing an option). Creative-thinking techniques (brainstorming, mind-maps) generate the options.

atomic_skills.title: Business opportunity, research & SWOT
atomic_skills.description: Developing a research instrument and assessing needs and desires; identifying business opportunities from researched needs; research instruments and data collection (questionnaires, interviews); research protocol/ethics; and applying a SWOT analysis to assess a viable venture.

error_signatures.description: Misplaces a SWOT factor (internal vs external, positive vs negative)
error_signatures.example: Lists a new competitor as a 'weakness' instead of a 'threat'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: SWOT: Strengths & Weaknesses are INTERNAL (inside the business); Opportunities & Threats are EXTERNAL (outside). Strengths/Opportunities help; Weaknesses/Threats harm.

atomic_skills.title: Business location factors
atomic_skills.description: Factors that impact business location decisions: labour regulations, environmental factors, transport, infrastructure, cost of electricity and water, potential market, raw materials, labour market, climate, government/local regulations and taxes, and crime.

error_signatures.description: Cannot match a business type to the location factor that matters most for it
error_signatures.example: Says a mine should locate near its customers rather than near the ore

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Match the factor to the business: raw-material businesses locate near materials; service businesses locate near customers; factories weigh transport and labour costs.

atomic_skills.title: Contracts & legal implications
atomic_skills.description: Definition of a contract and the types relevant to business — employment, insurance, lease, hire-purchase and rental agreements — with the parties to each and their rights and responsibilities under the relevant Acts.

error_signatures.description: Mismatches the parties to a contract
error_signatures.example: Calls the parties to a lease the 'insurer' and 'insured'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Learn the pair for each contract: employment = employer/employee; insurance = insurer/insured; lease = lessor/lessee; hire-purchase = seller/buyer; rental = landlord/tenant.

atomic_skills.title: Presentation of information
atomic_skills.description: Accurate, succinct verbal and non-verbal presentation of business information: reports with tables, graphs, diagrams and illustrations; verbal presentations with support materials (handouts, slides, charts); and the design and layout of a presentation using visual aids.

error_signatures.description: Confuses verbal with non-verbal presentation formats
error_signatures.example: Calls a bar graph a verbal presentation

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Verbal = spoken/words (a talk, a report's text). Non-verbal = visuals (tables, graphs, diagrams, pictures). Good presentations put the most important information first and keep visuals clear.

atomic_skills.title: The business plan
atomic_skills.description: Development of a financially viable business plan: its components (cover page, executive summary, description of the business, vision/mission, ownership, product/service, legal requirements), SWOT analysis, and the marketing plan (market research and the marketing mix — the 4 or 7 Ps).

error_signatures.description: Cannot identify the purpose of a business plan component
error_signatures.example: Says the executive summary lists the owner's personal hobbies

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A business plan proves the venture is viable. Know each component's job: executive summary = short overview; marketing plan = how you reach customers (the Ps); financial analysis = does it make money.

atomic_skills.title: Self-management
atomic_skills.description: The concept of self-management and its relevance in business: time management, personal goals, a balanced lifestyle, developing a professional image, personal analysis of strengths/weaknesses/talents, and concepts of self-knowledge, self-confidence, stress management and adaptability.

error_signatures.description: Confuses self-management with being managed by others
error_signatures.example: Says self-management means waiting for a supervisor to give instructions

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Self-management = managing yourself: your time, goals, image and stress, without being told. It is the foundation for managing others later.

atomic_skills.title: Relationships & team performance
atomic_skills.description: How people work together to accomplish business objectives and the factors that influence these relationships (prejudice, beliefs, values, diversity); interpersonal relationships in the workplace; and the criteria for successful, collaborative team performance.

error_signatures.description: Cannot distinguish a criterion for good teamwork from a barrier to it
error_signatures.example: Lists 'prejudice' as a criterion for successful teamwork

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Good teams share: clear goals, openness, mutual respect and trust, commitment, sound relations. Barriers are the opposite: prejudice, poor communication, distrust. Diversity is a strength when managed well.

levels.title: Grade 11 — Business Studies
levels.description: Deepens all four CAPS knowledge areas. T1: influences and control over the three environments, their challenges and how a business adapts; socio-economic issues and industrial relations; sector links; the company vs other ownership forms; ways of acquiring a business. T2: advanced creative thinking; stress/crisis/change management; turning a business plan into an action plan; setting up a venture; professionalism & ethics; presenting information. T3: entrepreneurial success factors; citizenship; the marketing and production functions. T4: team dynamics & conflict; introduction to Human Resources. 19 atomic skills, progression-gated in CAPS teaching order.

tiers.title: Term 1 — Business environments, socio-economic issues, sectors, ownership & acquiring a business

atomic_skills.title: Influences and control over the three environments
atomic_skills.description: The degree of control a business has over the micro (full control), market (no control, only influence) and macro (no control) environments, and ways to be involved in the macro environment when it benefits the business.

error_signatures.description: Believes a business can control the market or macro environment
error_signatures.example: Says a business controls inflation

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Control shrinks as you move out: micro = control, market = influence only, macro = no control (adapt). A business can still get involved in the macro environment (e.g. lobbying) when it helps.

atomic_skills.title: Challenges of the micro, market and macro environments
atomic_skills.description: Identifying the challenges of each environment: micro (difficult employees, lack of vision, weak management, strikes), market (competition, supply shortages, changing consumer behaviour) and macro (legislation, income changes, globalisation, socio-economic issues).

error_signatures.description: Places a challenge in the wrong environment
error_signatures.example: Calls a difficult employee a macro-environment challenge

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Sort the challenge by where it comes from: inside the business = micro (staff, vision, management); close outside = market (competitors, suppliers, customers); broad outside = macro (laws, economy, globalisation).

atomic_skills.title: Adapting to environmental challenges
atomic_skills.description: How a business adapts to challenges of the three environments: information management, strategic responses, mergers/takeovers/acquisitions/alliances, organisation design and flexibility, social responsibility, and lobbying, networking and power relationships.

error_signatures.description: Confuses lobbying, networking and power relationships
error_signatures.example: Calls finding new customers 'lobbying'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Lobbying = influencing decision-makers/regulators. Networking = building useful contacts (e.g. new customers). Power relationships = strategic alliances and persuading big investors. All are ways to cope with an environment the business cannot control.

atomic_skills.title: Socio-economic issues & industrial relations
atomic_skills.description: The impact of contemporary socio-economic issues (inflation, economic crime, ethical misconduct, population growth, illiteracy, resource exhaustion, piracy, strikes) on business operations, and developments in industrial relations: labour strikes/go-slows/lockouts, the Labour Relations Act, and the nature, history, roles and functions of trade unions.

error_signatures.description: Cannot state the role of a trade union
error_signatures.example: Says a trade union represents the employer

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A trade union represents workers — it negotiates wages and conditions and protects members. Socio-economic issues hit business through cost and productivity. A go-slow is working slowly; a lockout is the employer shutting workers out.

atomic_skills.title: Links between the business sectors
atomic_skills.description: Investigating the links between primary, secondary and tertiary enterprises — how raw materials from primary enterprises flow to secondary enterprises that process them and to tertiary enterprises that distribute and service them.

error_signatures.description: Cannot trace a product through the sectors
error_signatures.example: Says a bakery (secondary) is a primary enterprise

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Follow the chain: primary extracts (farm grows wheat) → secondary processes (mill and bakery make bread) → tertiary sells/services (shop sells the bread). Each sector depends on the one before it.

atomic_skills.title: A company vs other forms of ownership
atomic_skills.description: The benefits and challenges of establishing a company versus a sole trader, partnership, close corporation or co-operative (including taxation), and the formation of companies — the Memorandum of Incorporation, the company name, incorporation and the prospectus.

error_signatures.description: Misses limited liability and separate legal identity as company benefits
error_signatures.example: Says a company owner is personally liable for all company debts

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A company is a separate legal person with limited liability and continuity, but more paperwork and tax. A sole trader/partnership is simpler but has unlimited liability. Weigh capital, liability, tax and continuity.

atomic_skills.title: Avenues of acquiring a business
atomic_skills.description: Ways of acquiring a business — franchising, outsourcing and leasing — with their advantages, disadvantages and contractual implications (e.g. royalties, legalities).

error_signatures.description: Confuses franchising, outsourcing and leasing
error_signatures.example: Says franchising means renting equipment

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Franchising = buy the right to trade under a proven brand (pay royalties). Outsourcing = pay another firm to do a task for you. Leasing = rent an asset instead of buying it.

tiers.title: Term 2 — Creative thinking, stress & change, action plans, setting up, ethics & presentation

atomic_skills.title: Creative thinking & problem-solving (advanced)
atomic_skills.description: Applying creative thinking to address business problems and improve practice: routine vs creative thinking, mental blocks to creativity, more complex techniques (Delphi, force-field analysis), working with others to generate ideas, and conventional vs non-conventional (including indigenous) solutions.

error_signatures.description: Confuses routine thinking with creative thinking
error_signatures.example: Calls following a fixed procedure 'creative thinking'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Routine thinking follows known steps; creative thinking breaks the pattern to find new ideas. Mental blocks (fear of failure, assuming one right answer) stop creativity. Techniques like brainstorming and Delphi help generate options.

atomic_skills.title: Stress, crisis & change management
atomic_skills.description: Concepts relating to stress (and how to manage it), the importance of stress management in pressurised workplaces, crisis management (tight deadlines, loss of property, illness), and theories of change management — dealing with and adapting to change such as retrenchment, globalisation and affirmative action.
atomic_skills.caps_topic: Stress, crisis, change and conflict management

error_signatures.description: Confuses stress, crisis and change management
error_signatures.example: Says a crisis is the same as everyday stress

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Stress = pressure on a person (manage with time management, exercise, support). Crisis = a sudden serious threat to the business. Change management = leading people through change so they adapt rather than resist.

atomic_skills.title: From business plan to action plan
atomic_skills.description: Transforming a business plan into an action plan using planning tools — Gantt charts and a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) with timelines and responsibilities — so that the plan becomes a sequence of dated, assigned tasks.

error_signatures.description: Confuses a business plan with an action plan
error_signatures.example: Says a Gantt chart belongs in the executive summary

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A business plan says WHAT and WHY; an action plan says WHO does WHICH task by WHEN. A Gantt chart shows tasks against a timeline; a WBS breaks the work into smaller tasks.

atomic_skills.title: Setting up a business venture
atomic_skills.description: Initiating and setting up a business venture based on an action plan to generate income, and acquiring funding where needed — equity capital, loans/debt and other sources of capital.

error_signatures.description: Confuses equity capital with loan (debt) capital
error_signatures.example: Says a bank loan is equity capital

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Equity capital = the owner's own money or money from investors (no repayment, but shared ownership). Loan/debt capital = borrowed money that must be repaid with interest.

atomic_skills.title: Professionalism & ethics
atomic_skills.description: The theories and principles of professionalism and ethics and how they relate to business: the definitions of and differences between professionalism and ethics, good vs bad decisions, the concept of ethics and different perspectives on it, and the skills of professional, responsible, ethical and effective business practice.

error_signatures.description: Confuses professionalism with ethics
error_signatures.example: Says being on time is an example of ethics

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Ethics = doing what is morally right (honest, fair). Professionalism = the standard of conduct in your work (reliable, respectful, competent). You can be professional and still face an ethical choice.

atomic_skills.title: Presentation & responding to feedback
atomic_skills.description: Accurate, succinct verbal and non-verbal presentation of business information (tables, graphs, diagrams, posters, handouts), written information such as reports and flyers, and responding to questions and feedback in a non-aggressive, professional manner.

error_signatures.description: Responds unprofessionally to questions
error_signatures.example: Says you should argue with anyone who criticises your presentation

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: When questioned: answer all questions, make notes, do not argue, and apologise for any errors. Put the most important information first and keep visuals clear.

tiers.title: Term 3 — Entrepreneurial success, citizenship, marketing & production functions

atomic_skills.title: Entrepreneurial qualities & success factors
atomic_skills.description: Assessing the degree to which a business embraces entrepreneurial qualities (risk-taking, perseverance, good management) and critically reflecting on a venture to identify its key success factors (sustainability, profitability, customer base) and areas for improvement.

error_signatures.description: Cannot identify a key success factor
error_signatures.example: Says the colour of the logo is a key success factor

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Key success factors are the things that make a business work: a loyal customer base, profitability, sustainability and good management. Judge a venture against the entrepreneurial qualities, then name what to improve.

atomic_skills.title: Citizenship roles & responsibilities
atomic_skills.description: The citizenship roles and responsibilities business practitioners perform: how citizens, through business, contribute to the social and economic development of their communities, the concept of the business community, and the role of business, civil society, NGOs and CBOs.

error_signatures.description: Confuses an NGO with a CBO or with a government department
error_signatures.example: Says an NGO is a government body

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NGO = non-governmental organisation (independent, often national). CBO = community-based organisation (local). Business practitioners are citizens who can give time and effort to develop their communities.

atomic_skills.title: The marketing function
atomic_skills.description: Aspects of the marketing function: marketing activities, product policy (development, design, packaging, trademarks), pricing policy (techniques, factors, adjustments), distribution policy (channels, intermediaries, direct/indirect), communication policy (advertising, sales promotion, publicity, personal selling) and foreign marketing (imports and exports).

error_signatures.description: Assigns an activity to the wrong marketing policy
error_signatures.example: Calls choosing a delivery channel a 'pricing policy' decision

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Tie the activity to its policy: product = design/packaging/brand; pricing = setting the price; distribution = getting it to the customer (channels); communication = telling customers about it (advertising, selling).

atomic_skills.title: The production function
atomic_skills.description: Aspects of the production function: production systems (mass, batch, job), production planning and control (planning, routing, scheduling, loading; dispatching, follow-up, inspection, corrective action), safety management (the Occupational Health and Safety Act), quality control (SABS), and production cost calculations (total cost, unit cost, selling price, profit, break-even).

error_signatures.description: Confuses the three production systems
error_signatures.example: Says making one custom wedding dress is mass production

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Job = one custom item; batch = a group of identical items at a time; mass = continuous large-scale identical output. Break-even is where total income equals total cost — no profit, no loss.

tiers.title: Term 4 — Team dynamics, conflict & Human Resources

atomic_skills.title: Team dynamics & conflict management
atomic_skills.description: Team development stages (forming, storming, norming, performing), team dynamics theories (Belbin roles, Jungian insights, group consensus), and conflict management — causes of conflict, conflict-management theories and skills to resolve differences, and the function of workplace forums.

error_signatures.description: Misorders the team development stages
error_signatures.example: Says performing comes before storming

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Team stages in order: forming (getting to know each other) → storming (conflict) → norming (settling) → performing (working well together). Conflict managed well can strengthen a team.

atomic_skills.title: Introduction to Human Resources
atomic_skills.description: An introduction to the human resources function: recruitment, selection and interviewing procedures; the legalities of employment contracts; induction and placement; salary determination (piecemeal and time-related, including personal tax); and employee benefits (pension, medical, other). Relevant Acts: LRA, BCEA, EEA, COIDA.

error_signatures.description: Confuses recruitment with selection
error_signatures.example: Says recruitment means choosing the best candidate

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Recruitment = attracting applicants (advertising the post). Selection = choosing the best one (screening, interviewing). Induction = settling the new employee in. Each HR Act protects a different right.

levels.title: Grade 12 — Business Studies
levels.description: Final FET year, applying and evaluating across all four CAPS knowledge areas. T1: impact of recent legislation; the Human Resources function; ethics & professionalism; creative thinking in complex contexts; macro-environment business strategies. T2: social responsibility/CSR & CSI; human rights, inclusivity & environment; team performance & conflict; the business sector and its environment; management & leadership; quality of performance (TQM). T3: investment securities; insurance & assurance; forms of ownership and business success; presentation & data response. Term 4 is exam revision (no new content). 15 atomic skills, progression-gated in CAPS teaching order.

tiers.title: Term 1 — Legislation, Human Resources, ethics, creative thinking & business strategies

atomic_skills.title: Impact of recent legislation on business
atomic_skills.description: The impact of recent legislation, developed for redress and equity, on small and large business: the Skills Development Act, Labour Relations Act, Employment Equity Act, Basic Conditions of Employment Act, COIDA, BEE and BBBEE, National Credit Act and Consumer Protection Act — their nature, purpose, advantages/disadvantages, rights and compliance, plus human rights, inclusivity and environmental issues.

error_signatures.description: Matches an Act to the wrong purpose
error_signatures.example: Says the Consumer Protection Act sets the minimum wage

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Tie each Act to its purpose: EEA = fair, equal workplaces; BCEA = minimum working conditions; LRA = fair labour relations and unions; SDA = skills and SETAs; CPA = consumer rights; NCA = fair credit; BBBEE = economic redress.

atomic_skills.title: The Human Resources function
atomic_skills.description: Relevant legislation and the aspects of the human resources function: recruitment and selection; employee contracts; induction and placement; salary administration (piecemeal and time-related, including personal tax); employee benefits; and skills development (the Skills Development Act, SETAs, learnerships, the NQF and SAQA).

error_signatures.description: Confuses time-related and piecemeal salary determination
error_signatures.example: Says piecemeal pay means being paid by the hour

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Time-related pay = paid for time worked (hourly/monthly). Piecemeal pay = paid per unit produced. Recruitment attracts applicants, selection chooses, induction settles them in, and skills development grows them.

atomic_skills.title: Ethics & professionalism
atomic_skills.description: How professional, responsible, ethical and effective business practice should be conducted in changing and challenging environments: the meaning of ethical behaviour, ethical vs unethical and professional vs unprofessional practice with examples, the link between the two, and strategies to address issues such as taxation, sexual harassment, unfair advertising and abuse of work time.

error_signatures.description: Labels an unethical practice as ethical (or vice versa)
error_signatures.example: Says unfair advertising is an ethical business practice

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Ethical practice is honest and fair (pay fair wages, pay tax, advertise truthfully). Unethical practice harms others for gain (corruption, unfair ads, abusing work time). Professional behaviour supports ethical behaviour.

atomic_skills.title: Creative thinking in complex contexts
atomic_skills.description: Applying creative thinking and advanced problem-solving skills to respond to challenges in dynamic and complex business contexts and case studies, building on the problem-solving cycle and techniques from earlier grades.

error_signatures.description: Applies a single fixed solution to a complex problem
error_signatures.example: Says there is only one correct answer to every business problem

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Complex problems need creative thinking: generate several options, weigh them against the real business situation, and choose the best. Advanced problem-solving combines techniques rather than relying on one fixed answer.

atomic_skills.title: Macro-environment business strategies
atomic_skills.description: Devising strategies for how a business can respond to challenges of the macro environment, then evaluating them: SWOT-based strategy formulation, implementation and evaluation; integration strategies (forward, backward, horizontal), intensive strategies (market penetration, market and product development), diversification strategies, and defensive strategies (retrenchment, divestiture, liquidation).

error_signatures.description: Confuses the strategy types
error_signatures.example: Calls buying out a supplier 'market penetration'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Integration = take over another level (supplier = backward, distributor = forward, competitor = horizontal). Intensive = grow current/new products and markets. Diversification = move into new areas. Defensive = cut back (retrench, divest, liquidate).

tiers.title: Term 2 — CSR, human rights, teams, sector & environment, leadership & quality

atomic_skills.title: Social responsibility, CSR & CSI
atomic_skills.description: Critically examining social responsibility and its implications for business and communities: Corporate Social Responsibility (nature, process, benefits and challenges, components) and Corporate Social Investment (nature, projects, responsible business practice), and meaningfully contributing time and effort to others' well-being.

error_signatures.description: Confuses CSR with CSI
error_signatures.example: Says CSR and CSI mean exactly the same thing

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: CSR = the whole responsible way a business operates (ethics, environment, health and safety). CSI = the specific projects/money a business invests in communities (a part of CSR). Both go beyond what the law requires.

atomic_skills.title: Human rights, inclusivity & environment
atomic_skills.description: Evaluating the extent to which a business venture addresses human rights (as defined in the Constitution), inclusivity (diversity of poverty, inequality, race, gender, language, age, disability) and environmental issues (protecting the environment and human health), and assessing a venture against these criteria.
atomic_skills.caps_topic: Human rights, inclusivity and environmental issues

error_signatures.description: Confuses a human-rights issue with an environmental issue
error_signatures.example: Lists recycling as a human-rights issue

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Human rights = equality, dignity, fair treatment of people. Inclusivity = welcoming diversity (gender, race, disability, etc.). Environmental issues = protecting nature and health. Judge a venture against all three.

atomic_skills.title: Team performance & conflict management
atomic_skills.description: Collaborating to achieve objectives: criteria for successful team performance, self- and team-assessment against those criteria, performing a specific role in a team, problem-solving when working with others, correct procedures to deal with grievances, and ways of dealing with difficult people.

error_signatures.description: Does not know the correct grievance procedure
error_signatures.example: Says the first step in a grievance is to resign

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Successful teams share clear goals, trust, communication and commitment. Handle grievances through the correct steps (raise it, discuss, escalate if unresolved). Deal with difficult people calmly and professionally.

atomic_skills.title: Business sector and its environment
atomic_skills.description: Selecting a business from each economic sector and describing the three business environments related to those sectors and the extent to which a business can control each environment.

error_signatures.description: Says a business controls its macro environment regardless of sector
error_signatures.example: Says a mining business controls global commodity prices

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Whatever the sector (primary, secondary, tertiary), the rule holds: full control of the micro environment, influence over the market, no control over the macro environment.

atomic_skills.title: Management & leadership
atomic_skills.description: Differentiating between management and leadership styles and approaches: the difference between leadership and management, leadership styles (democratic, autocratic, etc.), theories of management and leadership (situational, transactional, transformational), and the role of personal attitude in success and leadership.

error_signatures.description: Confuses management with leadership
error_signatures.example: Says management and leadership are exactly the same

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Management = planning, organising and controlling the work. Leadership = inspiring and influencing people toward a vision. Autocratic leaders decide alone; democratic leaders involve the team.

atomic_skills.title: Quality of performance & TQM
atomic_skills.description: How the quality of performance within the business functions influences the success or failure of a business: the concept of quality, its relation to the various functions, and the elements of Total Quality Management (TQM) — continuous skills development, total client satisfaction and continuous improvement of processes and systems.

error_signatures.description: Treats quality as only the product's job, not TQM across the business
error_signatures.example: Says TQM only applies to the production function

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: TQM means everyone in every function continuously improves quality: total client satisfaction, ongoing skills development and constant improvement of processes. Poor quality in any function can sink the business.

atomic_skills.title: Investment: securities
atomic_skills.description: A range of business investment opportunities: business investments and the JSE, types of shares, unit trusts and government retail bonds; returns such as dividends and interest; and calculations including the difference between simple and compound interest.

error_signatures.description: Confuses simple and compound interest, or dividends and interest
error_signatures.example: Says compound interest is calculated only on the original amount

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Simple interest is on the original amount only; compound interest is on the amount plus past interest, so it grows faster. Shares pay dividends (a share of profit); savings/bonds pay interest.

atomic_skills.title: Investment: insurance & assurance
atomic_skills.description: Distinguishing assurance from insurance, compulsory and non-compulsory insurance, life insurance and retirement annuities, insurance of goods, the principle of average with over- and under-insurance calculations, and the compulsory funds — the Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) and Road Accident Fund (RAF).

error_signatures.description: Confuses assurance with insurance, or compulsory with non-compulsory
error_signatures.example: Says car insurance is assurance because the event is certain

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Assurance covers an event that WILL happen (death) — e.g. life cover. Insurance covers an event that MIGHT happen (fire, theft). UIF and RAF are compulsory. Under the principle of average, under-insuring means you are paid out proportionally less.

atomic_skills.title: Forms of ownership & business success
atomic_skills.description: Determining the extent to which a particular form of ownership contributes to the success or failure of a business, recapping the characteristics, advantages, disadvantages and comparison of forms of ownership with a focus on capacity, taxation, management, capital, division of profits and legislation.

error_signatures.description: Cannot link a form of ownership to a success or failure factor
error_signatures.example: Says unlimited liability has no effect on a business's risk

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Judge a form of ownership by how it affects success: limited liability and continuity help a company raise capital and survive; unlimited liability and limited capital can hold a sole trader back. Match capital, tax, management and risk to the venture.

atomic_skills.title: Presentation & data response
atomic_skills.description: Accurate, succinct verbal and non-verbal presentation of business information, including the criteria for a logical and effective presentation, the process and style of using visual aids, responding professionally to questions and feedback, and amending plans and documents as necessary.

error_signatures.description: Ignores feedback instead of amending the work
error_signatures.example: Says you should never change a presentation after feedback

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: An effective presentation knows its audience, puts the most important information first, and uses clear visuals. After feedback, amend the plan and documents and carry the improvements into future work.
